children: is expanding Gemini's ability to act on behalf of users, testing a feature that can call businesses to make reservations, check product availability, and reschedule appointments, putting its AI assistant into an increasingly competitive market for personal agents.

The feature, called Agentic Calling, allows Gemini to place calls from a user's own phone number and conduct conversations using an AI-generated voice, according to terms published by the company on Thursday.
The feature comes as technology companies, including Meta Platforms
, push AI agents beyond answering questions toward completing tasks for users. Meta's Muse, launched earlier this month, can also make calls to businesses on behalf of users.
Gemini can navigate automated phone menus, wait on hold, and speak with business representatives. Users can monitor calls through a live transcript and take over the conversation at any point.

said Gemini will identify itself as a Google AI assistant at the beginning of every call and disclose that the call is being recorded. Users must provide accurate identity and contact information for Gemini to share during calls.

The feature is limited to personal use and cannot be used for emergency calls, political messages, unsolicited telemarketing, or calls on behalf of businesses, government agencies, or law enforcement. Google
also prohibits users from transmitting personal or sensitive health information through the feature.
cautioned that Gemini may misinterpret responses or provide inaccurate information and said it does not guarantee that every call will successfully complete its intended task.
Calls use the user's cellular network and phone number, with standard carrier charges applying, Google
